title: Two weeks of repetitive gut-challenge reduce exercise-associated gastrointestinal symptoms and malabsorption
authors: Miall A, Khoo A, Rauch C, Snipe RMJ, Camoes-Costa VL, Gibson PR, Costa RJS
journal: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
population: Endurance runners (n = 18) randomised to blinded CHO (90 g/h) or placebo gut-training for 2 weeks
findings: Gut-training: 1 h running at 60% VO2max-equivalent daily for 2 weeks while consuming 90 g CHO/h (CHO) or 0 g/h (PLA).
In the repeat 2 h gut-challenge, gut discomfort (P = .012), total (P = .009), upper (P = .015) and lower GI symptoms (P = .008) and nausea (P = .05) were reduced on CHO but not PLA.
Peak breath H2 fell from 13 +/- 6 to 6 +/- 3 ppm on CHO (P = .004) but not PLA; feeding tolerance did not differ between trials.
Effort-bout distance rose from 11.7 +/- 1.5 to 12.3 +/- 1.3 km on CHO only (P = .035).
limitations: Very small (n = 18), 2-week laboratory-style protocol, 1 h daily sessions, no ultra-distance or solid-food outcomes; Crossref lists online publication in 2017, print year 2018 used here.
implications: Gut-training pathway default: about 14 days of near-daily 1 h steady runs at the target race CHO rate (this protocol used 90 g/h), only for athletes who choose a high-CHO race plan; lower-rate athletes can scale the rate to their own target.
Expect symptom and malabsorption benefits to show within 2 weeks; log symptoms to confirm per athlete.
Evidence is low-certainty; do not present it as guaranteed.

verification.notes: Crossref title/journal/authors match (issued year 2017 online, Europe PMC 2018 print); all numbers from Europe PMC abstract. Added by verifier as a second gut-training RCT.
